Hope you’re well — we have an immediate need to increase our reserved capacity by roughly 40% for the next 3 months due to a patient-intake spike. Can you send the pricing options (one-off top-up vs. re-annualize), any minimums, and what kind of approval turnaround/timeframes you need from our side? Procurement attached our standard procurement_form.pdf for reference. We’re aiming to make a decision by Dec 15 if there’s an attractive path.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Katie Barnes <katie.barnes@fortishealth.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 18:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle capacity ask + packaging options

Hi Katie — thanks for the context and the form. Quick summary of two pragmatic paths we typically offer: 

- Option A — Short-term top-up: add the extra capacity as a timeboxed top-up for 3 months at list price with a transient operational discount (we can do up to 10% off list on short-term top-ups depending on timing). This is the fastest path and keeps your current contract unchanged.

- Option B — Re-annualize/co-term: migrate the uplift into an amended annual commit (annualized baseline increases) and co-term your contract to align the new baseline. For that we offer a step discount (example: 15% off the incremental units for customers that commit to a higher annual run rate and co-term). This requires an amendment and PO; typical legal/finance lead time is 1–2 weeks.

A couple of notes: we can only approve discounts beyond standard guidance with a short internal review (finance & legal signoff). If you’re looking for pricing that’s between these extremes (e.g., partial annualize + temporary top-up) we can structure a hybrid.

I’ll propose a draft mutual_action_plan.xlsx with timing and a recommended option. If you prefer, we can lock pricing if PO is received by Dec 15 — otherwise pricing is subject to capacity shelf pricing at the time of purchase.

Would you like me to prepare a concrete quote for both options?

Best,
Rishi
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
